rationale: ESOC25-825 uses banana as an example of a personalized vocabulary noun. Musa is a given name elsewhere. No banana intake or sensory exposure was tested.
Basil occurs as a given name in the author list and disclosures of the thrombectomy-trials member. No basil food or herb exposure appears.
A cherry-red retinal spot is a finding in the ocular ischemia case report. No cherry exposure is studied.
Cod. 75 is a neurorehabilitation service identifier. The study does not expose participants to cod or cod products.
ESOC25-2386 studies coffee intake and timing in 598 adults with cryptogenic ischemic stroke. Its outcome is stroke onset, without a measured fatigue contrast or Parkinson population.
Date and dates identify calendar timing, follow-up, and analytical landmarks in the regular collection. No date-fruit exposure is identified.
Fig and Figs identify numbered or lettered figures in different members. The fig fruit and Ficus aliases have no matching exposure.
The full regular abstract body has no identified lemon balm or Melissa officinalis exposure. The separate symptom and stroke outcomes do not establish a tea comparison.
ESOC25-825 lists lentils as an example of a personally useful food noun in aphasia therapy. No lentil intake, tasting or sensory intervention occurs.
The OATS-I consortium and Older Australian Twins Study supply acronym matches. There is no oat exposure in those members.
Orange identifies a university affiliation location in the exercise-expectations presentation. The body supplies no orange fruit or juice exposure.
Sage and Salvia occur as surnames in distinct abstracts and their disclosures. No sage food, tea or extract exposure is described.
Cherry Hill appears in an institutional affiliation on the typhoid-fever member. It has no cherry intake or preparation comparison.
An emergency case notes chicken breeding as the patient's occupation. No chicken intake, food preparation or attributable chicken-specific effect is investigated.
Cinnamon is a faculty member's given name in the outreach elective presentation. There is no cinnamon preparation or extract exposure there.
Codfish vertebra describes the imaging shape of vertebral bodies in kidney-related bone disease. The report measures no cod ingestion.

The PDF documents caffeine as a constituent in a combined analgesic and workout-supplement case contexts. Coffee-ground emesis refers to appearance. No member tests brewed coffee and Parkinson fatigue.
A bee sting occurred while the patient worked on a cranberry marsh. The case describes a setting, without cranberry ingestion or a berry-specific exposure effect.
The dated results, date fields and follow-up timing are calendar uses. The complete PDF identifies no date-fruit preparation or exposure.
The fig matches refer to figures rather than Ficus carica or edible fig products. No fig exposure was verified in the complete supplement.
The original supplement did not identify lemon balm, Melissa officinalis or balm-mint use. Symptom reports in other members do not establish an ingredient comparison.
Onion is an author's surname in the forensic asylum evaluations abstract. The member does not study onion consumption.
Orange appears in locations and as a urine-color description. The collection has no confirmed orange fruit or juice exposure in these passages.
Rosemary is an author's given name in the levothyroxine adjustment presentation. It does not denote an ingested herb.
Salmon-colored describes a rash in a clinical vignette. The complete supplement gives no salmon intake comparison for the reviewed claims.
